Proposed: one product repository, agreed application scope

rect.data-content:
Web interface and core APIs
tl-lms-ui; tl-lms-service; tl-auth-service

AI tools, chat and tutor

tl-grading-service

Content, files and scheduled jobs

Adjacent scope to decide
tl-lms-db; tl-oss-components; tl-file-ingestion-pipeline
Confirm owners, operating paths and inclusion.
trek-learning/ Illustrative repository name; team to agree

apps/ and services/
Web UI plus service folders with their own build and test entry points.

packages/ and .github/
Shared libraries where justified, reusable CI, and affected-service checks.

db/ and supporting components, if included
Agree migrations, Keycloak image and ingestion-pipeline ownership.

docs/ and local development guidance
One onboarding path, clear contracts, service owners and release instructions.

g.textArea: Benefits to evaluate
Costs and constraints
Alternative to compare

rect.data-content:
• Review related UI/API changes together.
• Share tooling and local setup where useful.
• Make service contracts and owners easier to find.

• Dependency-aware CI and cache design take work.
• Shared changes can affect many services.
• Access, history and migration need agreement.

Keep service repositories separate and standardize
shared CI, contracts and onboarding. Compare
developer effort and release coordination with the team.

Scope accounting and proposal boundaries
16 is the product-group total: 11 application repositories, 3 adjacent candidates and 2 DevOps repositories.
Agree the home of tl-lms-gitOps and tl-trekai-terraform with Proposal 02. TrekCAP/TrekFinder belongs to Proposal 04. One repo does not require one release.

g.textArea: Evidence: Trek Learning product map and repository/delivery matrix, GitHub snapshot Nov 3, 2026. Candidate folders are proposed; final scope needs application-team review.

g.data-frame: 03B Trek Learning: developer and release workflow

rect.data-title: 03B Trek Learning: developer and release workflow

g.textArea: 03B Trek Learning: developer and release workflow
Developers / reviewers / QA / DevOps | Draft | Check affected services, publish identifiable images, and verify the selected release.
Blue = proposed | Gray = saved evidence or context | Yellow = tradeoff, exception or team decision

rect.data-content:
Saved baseline: application workflows build images and propose GitOps changes; Argo CD consumes the merged configuration.
The documented app branches are develop / staging / main, with rebuilds per environment. Successful current execution and enforcement remain unverified.

1. Propose a change
Edit UI, service or shared code.
Describe affected contracts
and migration needs.

2. Find affected services
Inspect paths and dependencies.
Include shared-code consumers.
Use broader checks if uncertain.

3. Test and review
Run relevant build/tests.
Check service compatibility.
Get affected-owner approval.

4. Merge and build
Build affected service images.
Record commit and image digest.
Keep service artifacts distinct.

5. Propose deployment
Update intended GitOps paths.
Identify services and target.
Follow agreed release approval.

6. Deploy and verify
Argo CD reconciles GitOps.
QA checks required journeys.
Record outcome and evidence.

Checks fail or review requests changes
Block merge; return findings to the author.
Revise, then rerun the affected checks and review.

Deployment or acceptance fails
Stop further promotion; owners investigate.
Use the agreed recovery path and record results.

g.textArea: Checks follow dependencies, not just changed folders
A shared commit can still produce separate releases

rect.data-content:
• Test changed services and their shared-code consumers.
• Check UI/API contracts and schema compatibility.
• Recheck all consumers of shared build configuration.
• Treat unclear impact as a reason for broader validation.

• Each service keeps an identifiable image and release record.
• Coordinate dependent releases when contracts change.
• Agree database migration order and recovery separately.
• A green build does not prove the deployed journey works.

Agree the release contract with application developers
Choose branch/version strategy, required checks, review owners, QA evidence and deployment gates.
Coordinate GitOps location with Proposal 02; release-policy simplification belongs to Proposal 11. Monorepo migration does not require changing branch policy.
Terraform execution remains Proposal 01; application branches do not define the Terraform environment target.

g.textArea: Basis: sourced repository/delivery matrix, Nov 3–4 snapshots; static GitOps review Nov 6. The affected-service workflow and release evidence above are proposed improvements.
03C Trek Learning: monorepo delivery plan
Application developers / QA / DevOps | Draft | Agree scope together, prove a small migration, and expand after the release path is verified.
Blue = proposed | Gray = saved evidence or context | Yellow = tradeoff, exception or team decision
Proposed work packages

rect.data-content:
1. Understand the product code
Confirm the 11 application repositories.
Map contracts, shared code and releases.
Decide which adjacent components belong.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: Application leads + DevOps

rect.data-content:
2. Agree how the team will work
Compare monorepo and shared standards.
Choose folders, owners, tests and access.
Define local setup and release boundaries.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: Application team + DevOps

rect.data-content:
3. Prove one small migration
Choose a manageable service or service pair.
Verify local setup, CI and a dev release.
Rehearse source cutover and recovery.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: App owners + QA + DevOps

rect.data-content:
4. Move the rest step by step
Move agreed groups with their history.
Switch consumers to the new locations.
Retire old write paths after acceptance.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: App owners + DevOps
Evidence before expanding
References and automation to update
Cutover and recovery
Decisions with application developers

rect.data-content:
• Build and test a changed service without rebuilding all.
• Show a shared change checks every known consumer.
• Trace commit → image digest → GitOps → dev outcome.
• Verify selected user journeys and migration compatibility.

• Checkout paths, Docker contexts, tests and cache keys.
• Workflow triggers, image names and GitOps writers.
• Ownership/review rules, identities and security checks.
• Local setup, documentation and operational entry points.

• Agree history, open-PR handling and a cutover window.
• Keep one writable source per migrated service.
• Rehearse restoring build/deploy references if needed.
• Plan application recovery and data migration handling.

• Confirm application, database, Keycloak and pipeline scope.
• Agree owners, access and shared-package boundaries.
• Choose affected-service tooling and required checks.
• Select pilot scope, acceptance evidence and recovery owner.

Keep code organization and deployment behavior explicit
Folder ownership does not isolate read access; retain separate repositories where visibility requires it. Migration does not make services one application.
Coordinate DevOps/GitOps changes with 02 and release-policy changes with 11. Dates, named owners, scope and implementation approval remain to agree.

g.textArea: Planning uses the existing Nov 3–4 inventory. Database execution and ingestion-pipeline delivery need owner confirmation. Candidate ownership and acceptance criteria require team agreement.
